source_review.notes: Reviewed eight references for microservice characteristics, bounded contexts, Conway's law, deployable application practices, SRE, team cognitive load, incremental replacement, and microservice design. Official or author-maintained linked endpoints were checked at review time; the O'Reilly landing page returned access-control HTTP 403 after resolving, while the other linked sources returned HTTP 200. The 2025 Team Topologies second-edition title and publication metadata were verified against the publisher's current page.

evidence: Reviewed service dependency graph, edge annotations, release sets, coordination rate, series availability, operation-attempt identity, and authoritative outcome notation.
Confirmed subsets, cardinalities, products, powers, ratios, percentages, empty-window treatment, and independence assumptions are defined before use.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Release coupling, availability, retry amplification, and remote outcome remain separate models with explicit scope.

evidence: Recomputed Example 3 coordination rate as 18 divided by 20 equals 0.9.
Recomputed Example 4 as 0.999 to the twentieth power equals 0.9801888648295347, approximately 98.019 percent.
Recomputed Example 7 worst-case nested attempts as 3 to the fifth power equals 243.
Recomputed Exercise 2 as 0.997 to the eighth power equals 0.9762504936564124, approximately 97.6251 percent.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Availability calculations are explicitly diagnostic independent-series models, retry amplification is a stated worst case, and coordination rate has no asserted universal threshold.

evidence: Verified the equal independent all-required availability model reduces the unequal product to a power, A equals a to the n.
Verified coordination rate uses coordinated releases as a subset of all releases and defines an empty observation window as unavailable rather than zero.
Verified the remote-outcome argument keeps timeout observation distinct from authoritative not-received, committed, rejected, compensated, and manual states.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Relaxing independence, requiredness, equal availability, or stable observation-window assumptions is explicitly said to change the result.

evidence: Reviewed entity-per-service over-decomposition, isolated hostile image work, high release coupling, twenty-way hard fan-out, lost payment response, stale inventory projection, nested retry multiplication, shared domain-library coupling, dual-write migration, and regulated clinical isolation.
Checked shared writable data, cycles, version skew, rollback, message replay, lag, identity delegation, credential rotation, saturation, platform ownership, no-owner services, and service merging.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Examples include benefits, counterexamples, partial failures, security boundaries, migration, organizational constraints, and high-consequence operation.

evidence: Traced capability, deployment, data, remote outcome, fan-out, release coupling, team, resource, security, and evidence invariants through exposition and exercises.
Confirmed process separation does not substitute for contract, data, release, team, security, or operational independence.
invariant_checking.notes: The modular monolith remains a credible alternative and poor service splits are explicitly reversible.

evidence: Reviewed the fan-out derivation under independent equal availability and all-required success; multiplication yields a to the n and changes when assumptions change.
Reviewed the ambiguous remote-outcome argument and confirmed timeout can be compatible with both nonreceipt and commit.
Confirmed no probability result is generalized to correlated production dependencies or an end-to-end SLO.
proof_review.notes: The derivations are bounded to stated probability and observation models and do not claim empirical prediction.

evidence: Audited uses of independently deployable, authoritative, consistent, isolated, secure, available, compatible, complete, proof, and evidence.
Verified repositories, containers, meshes, contract tests, traces, SLOs, metrics, progressive rollout, and process boundaries retain explicit limitations.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No product label, platform mechanism, calculation, or test is presented as universal correctness or architectural quality.

empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The chapter proposes change, release, reliability, capacity, and operational measurements but presents no executed code, benchmark, production dataset, or reproduced empirical study.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed style definition, forces, capability boundaries, bounded contexts, team ownership, independent deployment, data authority, local transactions, consistency, interactions, dependency graphs, fan-out, retries, degradation, delivery platform, security, observability, tests, evolution, deployments, incidents, measures, migration, merging, SOA comparison, and modular-monolith alternatives for coherence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed release trains, shared writes, database-server versus schema ownership, read models, outbox, unknown outcomes, nested retries, dependency cycles, credential and data scope, platform tickets, rollout, rollback after state change, on-call load, dual-write cutover, last-known authority, and regulated separation. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified first-principles microservice vocabulary, four bounded quantitative and state models, sixteen misconceptions, ten distinct worked examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers ending in a city emergency-services transfer problem.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
